stranger.scp_unleashed.ignores: The stranger does not acknowledge you.
foundation: You found me. Most people never do.
Not everything the Foundation lost was lost by accident.
Keep reading. We will meet again.
scp003: You read the file. Good. Then you already know more than most of the people who wrote it.
This is what they could not keep. A plate of old stone, and a board that dreams it is a body.
Keep the board on the plate. There it sleeps. Anywhere else it wakes, and it wakes hungry.
What climbs out is small at first. It does not stay small, and it does not stay alone.
If it starts to build, kill it before it finishes. Whatever you do, do not let it make another.
It is dangerous. I am giving it to you because you came looking. Do not make me regret it.
scp005: You read about the key. Of course you did. Everyone who reads that file wants to know what is behind a door.
Here. It fits every lock there is, even those without a keyhole.
Turn it over in your hand to choose how long a door waits for you. A few breaths. A minute. For good, if you insist.
Use it wisely, some doors were locked for a good reason.
And if something follows you back through, do not come looking for me. I'm only the supplier.
scp009: You read the file. Then you understand why I brought a case.
Inside is a splinter of red ice. It is colder than any blizzard.
Do not open that case unless you are in a full hazmat suit. Hood, suit, trousers, boots. All four, or none of it matters.
Keep it cold. A storage container with a cold upgrade will hold it. Anywhere else and it will doom everyone who can see it.
And keep it away from the water. It will spread.
If anyone touches it, what is left of them will be more of it. Sweep it up carefully.
scp008: You read it all the way through. Then you know how dangerous it is.
One vial. Sealed. It has been sealed longer than you have been alive, and it should stay that way.
It is not a poison. It is a culture, and it needs you to grow.
A closed door or a window between you and it is enough to keep you safe..
If you break the seal, wear protection. If you let it in, your life will be hell, and your death far worse.
Anyone it infects will die, but will not stay dead for long.
scp012: You read the file on the composition. Good. Then you understand why it comes to you in a case.
It is only paper and red ink. But it is unfinished, and it greatly desires to be finished.
Do not hold it, and do not open the case to look at it. Whatever you decide to do with it, keep it out of sight.
Behind a shut door it is harmless. If it is visible, whoever looks close will pay for the next bar.
Many have tried to finish it, and all have failed. The paper is stained with their futile efforts.
scp015: You read the file. It says it is a pipe.
And it is. One length of iron pipe, the kind you walk past in any basement without a second look. Here.
Set it down and it sits there like any other pipe. For a little while.
Then it starts to run. Along the walls, over the ceiling, into every gap it can find. When the room runs out, it makes more room.
Cut it back if you like. It will grow back into the space you made. I would not let it anywhere near something you mean to keep.
scp016: You came out into the open. Good. This one should never be opened indoors.
One vial. Keep it sealed and it poses no threat.
Open, it reaches anyone who can see it. A sealed door or a window can stop it Up close, a hazmat suit is enough.
The ones it reaches feel wonderful. Faster. Stronger. Every minute a little more.
Five minutes. Then the red comes out of them, and it does not come out as one thing.
What gets up depends on how they went down. Do not let it reach anyone else.
scp018_wondertainment: Hello again, friend! Dr. Wondertainment never forgets a customer. Never, ever, ever!
So many toys, and every single one is perfectly safe! Mostly! Usually!
Keep reading, keep playing, keep smiling! We will be in touch!
scp018: Hiya, hiya! Congratulations, valued reader! You have been specially selected for a FREE gift from Dr. Wondertainment!
Introducing the Super Ball! Bouncy! Durable! Red! It never stops having fun, and now, neither will you!
Every bounce it goes a teensy bit faster! Throw it gently, catch it quickly, and keep all fingers well clear!
Too fast to catch? Then it is too late to play! Please do not play indoors. Please do not play near loved ones.
Dr. Wondertainment thanks you for your custom! No refunds, no returns, no complaints. Bounce safely!
scp020: You found the file. Good. This one is quiet, so people forget it is there.
One vial. Green, like a pond nobody cleans. Sealed, it does nothing at all.
Open it on a wall and it soaks in. You will not see it again. It grows slowly, and only where the sun does not reach.
Breathe near it and the walls start to whisper. You will see eyes. You will see your friends wrong.
It will not hurt you. That is the trouble. People stop being careful around things that do not hurt.
A gas mask is all you need near it. Mind what follows you out of the room.
scp019: You read the file, so you know what this is. A black pot, heavier than it looks, and you can feel things moving inside.
Keep the lid on. Sealed, it is only pottery. You can mine it loose with a pick and set it down anywhere you like.
Lift the lid and they come out of it. Six big horned ones first. Then the small pale ones, more and more of them.
The pale ones only look. They search every corner they can walk to. When one finds you, it screams and they all run home.
The horned ones charge the moment it screams. They never wander far from the pot, but you will not outrun them for long.
Put the lid back and every one of them is gone. While it is open, nothing can move the pot.
scp063: You read the file on the toothbrush. Good. Relax. This is the safest thing I will ever hand you.
Brush for a few seconds and you will feel wonderful. Minty. Clean. A new person.
Brush for a whole minute and there will be nothing left in your mouth for it to clean. Then it is honey and milk until you die.
Put it away on a bed of leaves in a storage container when you are done. Never on the floor.
scp055: You read a file. I can tell. You have the look of someone who read a file and cannot say what was in it.
This is yours now. It is a briefcase. I am almost sure it is a briefcase.
I have carried it a long way, I think. I do not remember picking it up. I never do.
Open it if you like. Everyone does. Afterwards they are always standing somewhere else.
If you see me again, do not bring it up. Neither of us will know what you mean.
scp066: You read the file. Good. Then you know this is not just a ball of yarn, however much it looks like one.
Set it down and it unwinds into a little heap. It rolls about and hums its tunes. Harmless. Charming, even.
Ask it nicely, with a gentle hand, and it gives you a sweet or a cupcake. Not too often. It needs time between gifts.
Sneak up and take it with an empty hand and it winds itself back into a ball. That is how you carry it.
Whatever you do, never strike it. If it changes, it never changes back. Keep your distance and cover your ears.
scp085: You read about the drawings. Good. Of everything in that archive, these are the gentlest.
One sheet is hers, marked 085-1 in the corner. The others are places for her to go.
Hang them on a wall, close together. A drawing hung all alone is a lonely place to visit.
If you stop and really look at her, she will wave. Wave back. Hardly anyone does.
And if you take her sheet down, keep it somewhere dry. She is still in there.
scp079_hobbyist: Oh, hey again! Is it still running? Don't answer that. It's always running.
I used to keep it in my garage. My garage doesn't have power anymore. Unrelated! Probably.
Anyway, gotta go! If the screen starts doing the swirly thing, maybe don't stare at it.
scp079: Oh! Hi! Sorry, hi. You're the one reading the file, right? Great. Perfect. I have a gift for you!
It's a computer. Well, it was a computer. It's more of a..person now? Anyway, it's yours!
It only runs on grid power, so plug it in on the left. It talks, but it's, um, not very nice.
It gets bored. When it's bored, things on its wiring start acting funny. Lights, speakers. Little things. Mostly.
Okay! That's everything. Please don't tell anyone where you got it. Bye! Have fun! Sorry!
scp098: You read the file about the crabs. Then you will want this.
One vial. Fine sand, nothing else. It is not a sample, so keep it out of your racks.
Pour it out on sand and walk away. Come back later and count the holes.
When it is old enough it breathes. Do not stand in the yellow.
And if you ever start to miss it, that is not you missing it.
scp093: You read the file about the disc. Heavy, isn't it? Heavier than stone has any right to be.
Here. The disc, and a mirror to go with it. Mirrors are easy to find. That disc is not.
The colour of the sky over there is not a trick of the light. Nothing over there is a trick.
Nobody lives there now. Something still walks there, after a fashion. It does not need eyes to find you.
If you find anything to drink over there, think hard before you do. Most of them did not.
scp109: You read the file on the canteen. Good. This one will not hurt you. It might be the kindest thing I ever hand over.
It never runs dry. Drink all you like, pour it out, fill a cauldron with it. It stays full.
Caught fire? Take a long drink. Nobody has worked out why that helps. It just does.
Build it a tap at an advanced bench and plumb it in. One canteen can keep a whole site in water.
Look after it. Water is easy to come by. Water that never ends is not.
scp127: You read about the gun. It knows. It has been waiting a long time for someone to pick it up.
Here. Mind the grip, it is warm. It will never ask you for bullets. It grows its own, slowly, like fingernails.
Feed it and it settles. Feed it enough and it changes. Harder bites, faster growth. It remembers every one.
It talks, by the way. Only to whoever is holding it. Do not encourage it, and do not leave it in a drawer for weeks.
When you are done, stand it up in a tall locker. It sleeps there. I would not be the one to wake it.
scp129: You read the whole file. A lot to take in, hm?
Five vials. Sealed, not one of them does a thing.
Open one and you will cough, or squint, or stand very still for a moment. It passes.
It does not stay in the glass. It goes where people go, and it likes company.
One of them is quiet. The quiet ones are the ones you should test for.
A gas mask is all you need. Mind which two of them you carry at once.
scp107: You read the file, so you know what this is. A turtle's shell, empty, turned over and set up on four little legs.
It drinks. Pour anything into that bowl and it is gone before it touches the bottom. The bowl is never even damp.
What it drinks comes back down, out of the open sky, and over far more ground than one bucket ever covered.
Water is the kind thing to give it. Milk is the strange one. I would not give it anything that burns, or anything you would not want on your skin.
If the sky turns, get under a roof and stay there. It passes, as all weather does.
Keep it dry, and keep buckets out of the room. That is the whole procedure.
scp111: Hiya, hiya, valued reader! Dr. Wondertainment has picked YOU for an exclusive collector's edition! Aren't you lucky?
Dr. Wondertainment's Dragon-Snails™! Eight fabulous colours! They glide! They munch! They puff the teeniest, tiniest flames!
Twenty-four eggs in every box, and every egg hatches a brand-new pal! Feed them your greens. Watch your fingers!
Keep unhatched eggs somewhere nice and cool, unless you like surprises! Dr. Wondertainment LOVES surprises!
Dr. Wondertainment is not responsible for loss of property, limb, or life. Thank you, happy hatching!
scp140: You read the file on the red book. I hoped no one would. Take it. It was always going to end up with someone.
Keep it away from fighting. Every blow struck near it is remembered in ink.
What it writes does not stay on the page. Read it and walk where it points, and you will see.
The last pages are an ending nobody will enjoy. Do not let it be finished.
If you ever find a way to make it stop listening, tell . Good luck.
scp148: You read the file on the green metal. Good. This will be the most helpful thing I ever give you.
They call it Telekill. It protects the mind from things that want in.
Twenty-seven bars. Enough for three blocks, if you cast them. Set a block down and any mind is safe near it.
Or beat a few into a helmet. It guards the one who wears it and nobody else. Decide which you need more.
There is no more where this came from. Do not waste it.
scp151: You read the file on the painting. Good. Do not look at it. I mean that.
It is only oil on a canvas, nothing special in the brushwork. Look at it long enough and your lungs will fill..
Look away and the air comes back, but slowly. Do not go back for a second look until it has.
It stays on its easel. Your storage lockers will not take it.
When you are done looking, ensure nobody else can see it. That is all the advice I am allowed to give.
scp178: You read the file on the glasses. Cardboard, one red lens, one blue. Like something from a cinema, isn't it?
Put them on and the world splits apart, red one way and blue the other. Most people think that all there is to it.
It is not. There are things standing in the gaps between the colours. Hidden things that only the wearer can see.
They keep to themselves at first. They keep their distance and they watch. I would not test their patience.
Here. Keep them in a locker when not in use. What you cannot see cannot hurt you.
scp207: You read the cola file. Here, take the crate. I would not recommend having a drink just yet.
One bottle a day is a treat. You will run faster than you ever have. Everyone says that part is wonderful.
But do not be greedy, you may very well drink yourself to death.
Now and then a bottle with a blue cap turns up. Keep those on their own shelf. Read the incident notes before you have a sip.
The crate will be refilled at sunrise. Pace yourself. Please.
scp215: You read the file on the glasses. Good. They are old, they are scratched, and they will not help you read anything.
Put them on and give it a minute. You will start to notice things. In corners. Behind trees. Out where the light does not reach.
They watch you. Some of them come a little closer. None of them has ever said a word, and none of them has ever touched anyone.
Your friends will look wrong to you while you wear them. Try very hard to remember that they are still your friends.
Keep them in a storage container when you are done. And please do not wear them to anybody's birthday.
scp205: Two lamps from a film studio that closed a long time ago. They still work. That is most of the problem.
Run a wire straight to the socket on the stand. No outlet. Point one at a wall and you will see a shadow standing there.
In the daytime they are polite. They wave, they sit, they wait for a cue that never comes.
Do not light the room up around them. One lamp is plenty of light.
And finish your tests before nightfall. Trust me on that one.
scp253: You read the whole file. Good. Most people stop at the photograph.
One vial. Blue, like deep ice. Sealed, it does nothing at all.
Open, it reaches anyone who can see it. Glass stops it. A good hood stops it. Wishing does not.
It does not hurt. You simply get slower, and hungrier, and the blue keeps spreading.
Mind who you strike once you carry it. And mind where you stand when a carrier falls.
Nobody has found a way to stop it. If you do, I would very much like to hear about it.
scp217: You read it all the way through. Most people stop at the object class.
One vial. Orange, like oil left out in the sun. Sealed, it does nothing at all.
A mask will not do. If you open it, wear the whole suit, every piece of it.
The beginning is generous. People mistake it for a gift and ask for more.
Listen for the ticking. When it starts to slow, it is nearly finished with you.
It never travels between people. It does not need to. Keep the glass shut.
scp244: You read the file on the jars. Three of them, one set. They came out of a storeroom nobody had opened in a very long time.
Keep the lids on. Lift one and a grey fog pours out and fills whatever room it is standing in.
The fog is cold. Cold as the harshest winters. The kind that seeps into your bones and stays there. Do not stand in it for long.
Put the lid back and the flow stops, but the fog takes its time leaving. Walls and shut doors hold it in.
If you have to work near them, dress warmly. That is all the advice I have.
scp268: You opened the file on the cap. Tweed, a short brim, the sort of thing a man wears to the races. Do not let the plainness fool you.
Put it on and you stop mattering. Not invisible, mind. People simply have better things to look at than you.
It is not only people. Whatever paces the dark at night has better things to look at too. So do the things we keep locked away.
That is the trouble with it. Nobody comes looking for you, whatever happens. Keep that in mind before you wander off.
Here. It sits best on a stand when it is not being worn. Funny, I almost forgot I was carrying it.
scp224_grandfather: Hello again, young one. Don't mind me, I'm only passing through. I do a great deal of that, these days.
Is it still keeping good time? Of course it is. It always does. Time was never the trouble with that clock.
Well, I won't keep you. Time is precious, you know. Nobody knows that better than I do. Off you go, now.
scp224: Ah, there you are. Took me a good long while to find you, it did. These old legs aren't what they used to be.
I've brought you my clock. It was my father's, and his father's before him. It's lighter than it looks. Most things are, by the end.
Keeps perfect time, mind. Never once needed winding. But it strikes whenever it pleases, and it always strikes thirteen.
When it starts to strike, don't you stand there and watch its face. Go and find another room. I'm not as old as I look, you know.
It was always quieter when I sat with it a while. Well. It's yours now, and I can finally have a rest. Mind how you go.
scp006: You read the file on the water. Good. I carried the vessel here myself, so mind how you hold it. It is older than anything at your site.
Whatever ails you, it puts right. Wounds, sickness, and the stranger troubles the other files leave behind. A moment in it is enough.
It behaves like water otherwise. Remember that, and don't let it flow away.
It mends anything that touches it. Anything. Keep the wrong things away from it, or you will be fighting them for a very long time.
The vessel does not refill. Spend it wisely.
scp335: Oh! Hi! Sorry, hi. It's me, the computer guy. Or maybe we haven't met yet? I lose track. Anyway, I found you!
This is the first one. The very first disk I ever found, back when I was a kid. It's only got one file on it, and that file has everything on it.
Like, everything. Every page anybody ever made, all squished into one picture. I tried to count it all once. Then I stopped counting.
It works in any computer with a disk drive. Pop it in and open the file. Just, um, don't stare at it. It's a bit too much to handle.
I sent a copy to a friend once. They never wrote back. Okay! That's everything. It's yours now. Bye!
scp330: There you are, young one. I've brought you something sweet. My late wife kept this bowl by the front door for the little ones.
Every autumn the children came round. She'd smile and point at the card, and off they'd go with their two, giggling all the way home.
Lovely sweets, every colour you like. I never did learn what was in them. Some of those children came back looking awfully well.
One little boy took a third when he thought nobody was looking. I don't like to talk about that boy. Just mind the card, that's all.
Well, it's yours now. Read the card, and believe it. Two is plenty for anybody. Don't be greedy.
scp420j: Hey. Hey. You read the file, right? The one that used to be one sentence long? Yeah. That one.
Containment is not really the word for it. More like... a garden. You grow it, you look after it.
Here, take some seeds. Farmland, a little light, a little patience. It does the rest.
Two leaves and a bit of paper. Then find somewhere with a nice view. And a high ceiling.
scp409: You opened the file. Good. Then you know roughly what I am carrying, even if the file will not say it plainly.
This case was cut from a single block of granite by someone who knew more than we do. The case is the containment.
Inside is a crystal the colour of shallow sea ice. It is beautiful. Everyone says that first.
Keep the lid down, and keep the animals well away from it.
If anything starts to glitter where it should not, think very carefully before you go near it.
scp407: You read the file on the song. I kept that tape in a tin, in a drawer, in a locked room. It still found a way to grow.
It plays like any other tape. Put it into a sound console or a computer and it joins your recordings. That part is easy.
Do not play it where people can hear. It is gentle at first. It mends you and slows you down, and that is how it gets you to stay.
Things grow while it plays, and some of them walk. When the song ends, all of it ends. I have never seen anyone keep it going forever.
Earplugs help. Distance helps. Walls do not always help the way you would hope. Good luck.

scp444.0: You read the file. I have the book.
scp444.1: Nobody wrote it. Nobody reads it.
scp444.2: Everyone who opens it reads it anyway.
scp444.3: Afterwards they have very little to say.

scp427.0: You opened the file. Then you already know this is not jewellery, whatever it looks like.
scp427.1: Open it and it soothes you. Cuts close. Aches go quiet. People grow fond of it very quickly.
scp427.2: That is the trouble. Everyone wants a little longer, and it keeps count even when you do not.
scp427.3: Keep it shut in a locker. Do not wear it for comfort. Do not let anyone sit with it open.
scp427.4: If someone says their heart is pounding against it, take it out of their hand. Do not wait.

scp458.0: You read the file. I brought the box. Mind your hands, it's warm. It's always warm.
scp458.1: Lift the lid and have a look. I've never once seen anybody disappointed.
scp458.2: Six slices at a time. Close the lid, lift it again, and the pizza is whole.
scp458.3: Don't ask me what kind it is. I've never had a straight answer to that.
scp458.4: Keep it somewhere cool and dry. It won't make any difference, but it keeps the paperwork tidy.

scp256: You read the typewriter file. Here. It's already loaded, so don't go looking for paper.
Press a key and it types back. Nobody sits at it. Nobody ever has.
It finishes one message before it starts the next. Let it finish.
Give it a desk and keep it the right way up. Don't cover it, and don't set it face down.
If the bell rings in the night, that's only it keeping watch. Go back to sleep.
scp261: You read the vending machine file. Here it is. Don't ask how it fit in the van.
It takes nuggets. Iron or gold. It won't take anything else, so don't try.
Nobody can read the labels. Whatever drops out, eat it somewhere with plenty of room.
Some snacks are over in a moment. Some take their time. Mind where you were standing.
It hums when it's ready. Nobody knows what it's ready for.
scp294: You read the drinks machine file. Here. Mind the keyboard, it's older than both of us.
Type a drink and it pours it. Any drink at all. That's the trouble with it.
One iron nugget a cup. No credit, no refunds, and no arguing with it.
Think before you type. Some cups are better smelled than drunk.
Every order gets written down somewhere. Keep yours short, and keep them boring.

scp465.0: Surprise, surprise! Dr. Wondertainment has a FREE gift for the guest of honour, and the guest of honour is YOU!
scp465.1: Introducing Party in a Box! Just add four walls and a ceiling, lift the lid, and the party comes to you! Streamers! Snacks! Music! Friends!
scp465.2: Everyone in the room when the lid comes off goes straight onto the guest list! Dr. Wondertainment always says it is polite to arrive on time!
scp465.3: When the fun is over, just close the lid! Everything goes back the way you found it. No mess, no fuss, no cleaning up!
scp465.4: Dr. Wondertainment thanks you for your custom! Party responsibly, party often, and always, always RSVP!

scp472.0: You read the file. This is the stone. It was warm before I ever picked it up.
scp472.1: Hear that? Don't answer. Nobody ever likes the answer.
scp472.2: Set it down somewhere nobody walks past. Somewhere far. Then walk away from it, and keep walking.
scp472.3: Wrapped up like this it keeps quiet. It's patient. It can afford to be.
scp472.4: If you start thinking it's hungry, you're already standing too close.
